title: Kaliningrad: Russia's Piece of Germany
description:
Why does Russia own land between Poland and Lithuania? Kaliningrad was the German city of Königsberg, founded in 1255 by the Teutonic Knights. A king was crowned in its castle in 1701. British bombing burned the old centre in 1944, the Soviet Union captured it on 9 April 1945, and at Potsdam the Allies agreed in principle to transfer it to the Soviet Union. It was renamed Kaliningrad in 1946 after Mikhail Kalinin. Today every land link between the region and the rest of Russia crosses NATO and EU territory.

Full story: on our channel. The full video is "How Russia Ended Up Owning a Piece of Germany".
